Revision history: "This certificate is revision n°4 of OIML-MAA certificate R76/2006-FR2-14.01." Also the cert itself is "Rev.1". Hmm. The revision history — the certificate is Rev.1 of R76/2006-FR2-19.02, and it constitutes revision n°4 of OIML-MAA certificate R76/2006-FR2-14.01. I could record:
- revision "1" (Rev.1 of this cert number), date 2021-09-21, changes: revision n°4 of OIML-MAA certificate R76/2006-FR2-14.01.

Actually let me think. The certificate number is R76/2006-FR2-19.02 – Rev.1. The note says "This certificate is revision n°4 of OIML-MAA certificate R76/2006-FR2-14.01." So revision history could include:

Characteristics (type_level):
- intended accuracy class: III or IIII — this is a special one. "Usage prévu en classe: (III) (or) (IIII)". Could be a characteristic "accuracy_class" with value "III or IIII"? Hmm, the schema has recommendation.accuracy_classes. I'll put ["III", "IIII"] there. Also could add type_level characteristic "intended_use_class": value "III or IIII". Maybe keep it in recommendation only.

- Maximum number of weighing ranges: 2 in multi-range configuration; 3 in multi-interval configuration. This is config-dependent! Use config_level with axis "weighing_configuration":
  - {condition: "multi-range configuration", value: 2}
  - {condition: "multi-interval configuration", value: 3}

- Maximum number of verification scale intervals (n_ind): config-dependent:
  - class III single-interval (single range or multi-range): 6000 per weighing range
  - class IIII single-interval: 1000 per weighing range
  - multi-interval class III: 3000 per partial weighing range
  
  Use config_level with axis "instrument_configuration_and_class". Conditions:
  - "single-interval, class III, per weighing range": 6000
  - "single-interval, class IIII, per weighing range": 1000
  - "multi-interval, class III, per partial weighing range": 3000

- Maximum subtractive tare effect (T): "- Max" — hmm, value is "Max" (i.e., equals Max, 100% of Max?). The French "Effet maximal soustractif de tare (T) : - Max" means T = Max (subtractive tare effect up to Max). Value is symbolic "Max". Per rules, keep as string: {"value": "Max", "unit_symbol": null}. Actually "- Max" — probably "− Max"? It likely means T = -Max? No, typical is "T = +Max" for subtractive... Actually subtractive tare effect max = Max. I'll record value "Max" as string. Hmm "- Max" might be OCR of "= Max" or just a dash. I'll record value: "Max".

- Power supply voltage: 230 V AC (50 Hz) or battery 24 V
  - power_supply_voltage: {value: 230, unit_symbol: "V"}
  - power_supply_frequency: {value: 50, unit_symbol: "Hz"}
  - power_supply_type: "AC" — or alternative battery: voltage 24 V, type "battery (DC)". Could record:
    - power_supply_voltage: 230 V (mains) ... and config alternative? Maybe record two entries? The rules say split voltage/frequency/type. For battery: 24 V battery. I could record:
    - power_supply_voltage: {value: {min: 24, max: 230}, ...} — no, that's wrong. Better: record primary 230 V AC 50 Hz, and a second characteristic "alternative_power_supply_voltage": 24 V, "alternative_power_supply_type": "battery". Or use config_level with axis "power_supply": {condition: "mains", value: 230 V}, {condition: "battery", value: 24 V}. That seems clean. I'll do config_level:
      - attribute: power_supply_voltage, axis: power_supply_source, values: [{condition: "AC mains", value: 230, unit_symbol: "V"}, {condition: "battery", value: 24, unit_symbol: "V"}]
      And type_level: power_supply_frequency 50 Hz; power_supply_type "AC or battery".

  Simpler: type_level power_supply_voltage: 230 V; power_supply_frequency: 50 Hz; power_supply_type: "AC"; alternative_power_supply_voltage: 24 V; alternative_power_supply_type: "battery". Hmm, value 24 — number. I'll go with config_level approach for voltage and add type-level power_supply_type as "AC mains or 24 V battery". Actually let me not overcomplicate. I'll do:

  type_level:
  - power_supply_voltage: 230 V
  - power_supply_frequency: 50 Hz
  - power_supply_type: "AC"
  - alternative_power_supply_voltage: 24 V (battery)
  
  Hmm, the value must be object: {"value": 24, "unit_symbol": "V"}. And power_supply_type for battery... I'll add "alternative_power_supply_type": "battery".

  Actually config_level might be cleaner per rule 5. Let me use config_level:
  - attribute: "power_supply_voltage", axis: "power_source", values: [{condition: "AC mains", value: 230, unit_symbol: "V"}, {condition: "battery", value: 24, unit_symbol: "V"}]

  And type_level: power_supply_frequency 50 Hz, power_supply_type AC.

- Number of weighing channels: 1
- Load cell excitation voltage (E_exc): 5 V DC → value 5, unit "V", plus power_supply_type? It's DC. Record "load_cell_excitation_voltage": {value: 5, unit_symbol: "V"}. Maybe note DC in value? Keep unit V; the DC is the type. Could add to the value string? Rules say numbers not strings. I'll record value 5, unit "V". Maybe add "load_cell_excitation_type": "DC". Fine.

- Minimum input voltage per scale interval (ΔU_min): 0,5 μV → 0.5 μV. The markdown says "0, 5 μV" (weird spacing) — 0.5 μV. value 0.5, unit_symbol "μV".
- Measuring range minimum voltage: "0,0 mV" → 0.0 mV. value 0, unit "mV".
- Measuring range maximum voltage: 16 mV.
- Minimum load cell impedance (RL_min): 43,75 Ω → 43.75 Ω.
- Maximum load cell impedance (RL_max): 1245 Ω.
- Operating temperature range: -10°C / +40°C → {min: -10, max: 40}, unit "°C".
- Fraction of maximum permissible error p_ind: 0,4 → 0.4, dimensionless.
- Load cell connection: 6-wire shielded; type: PRECIA ref. 4005271 or similar; maximum length: 150 m (220 m for 1 mm² section); section: 0.68 mm².
  - load_cell_connection_type: "6-wire shielded"
  - load_cell_connection_cable_reference: "PRECIA ref. 4005271 or similar"
  - load_cell_connection_cable_maximum_length: config! 150 m standard, 220 m for 1 mm² section. So config_level with axis "cable_cross_section":
    - {condition: "0.68 mm² (standard)", value: 150, unit "m"}
    - {condition: "1 mm²", value: 220, unit "m"}
  - load_cell_connection_cable_cross_section: 0.68 mm².

Software version: identification scheme — first figure "1" for i…EDU versions, "2" otherwise. This is descriptive; could put in description or a characteristic "legal_software_version_identifier": "first digit '1' for i…EDU versions; '2' for all other versions". I'll include as type_level characteristic with string value.

Model family: The indicator has versions i20, i30, i35, i40, d20 — commercial designations of versions. These are model variants. Include model_family:
- family_name: "X112-B" (the type designation)? The family is X112-B with versions i20/i30/i35/i40/d20. family_name: "X112-B".
- models: [{"model_id": "i20", "label": "general use"}, {"model_id": "i30", "label": "appropriate for weighing bridges"}, {"model_id": "i35", "label": "appropriate for weighing bridges"}, {"model_id": "i40", "label": "weighing in a process"}, {"model_id": "d20", "label": "repeater"}]

Attributes per model? Housing mounting: table / cabinet back panel / front of housing — that's a configuration option, not per model. No numeric per-model attributes. So model_level characteristics probably not needed. But maybe not needed; schema says model_family included only if cert covers >1 model variant — yes it does.

Components: The indicator is a separate module intended to be connected to a weighing channel comprising analogue or digital strain gauge load cells. The load cells are not part of the certified type per se. I don't think components[] is needed here — the indicator itself is a single module. Skip components.
